newsitem.title: USA: Alaska wildfires are fanned by dry conditions.
newsitem.headline: Alaska wildfires are fanned by dry conditions.

text.p: Dry weather and gusty winds pose an extreme danger of wildfires through much of interior and south central Alaska, state and federal officials said Thursday.
Several campfires have already spread out of control despite a ban on open burning in most regions, said the Alaska Interagency Coordination Centre.
As of Thursday, 211 fires -- all caused by humans -- had burned 15,000 acres statewide, said Andy Williams, a spokesman for the interagency centre.
The fires included two small blazes in Big Lake north of Anchorage, the same area where a 37,000-acre fire last year destroyed more than 300 structures.

One of the fires began on the property of three-time Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race champion Martin Buser. Last year, Buser ferried his dogs by boat to islands in Big Lake to protect them from the flames.
The second Big Lake fire was considered a possible holdover from last year's blaze. Firefighters extinguished both Big Lake blazes.
As of Thursday, 17 of the fires were active and firefighters were deployed on four of them, Williams said. The other fires were being monitored, he said.
By Wednesday, they had controlled an 80-acre wildfire near Skwentna, a community without road access that is about 100 miles northwest of Anchorage.
